title: Add FP8/INT8 modes + stable warmup/measurement loops to runtime perf harness
author: Rina Kobayashi
content:
Title: Add FP8/INT8 modes + stable warmup/measurement loops to runtime perf harness

Context
We’re kicking off the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint and need the runtime perf suite to (a) run baseline vs FP8 vs INT8 apples-to-apples, (b) reduce run-to-run variance from inconsistent warmup and measurement, and (c) emit a standardized artifact format that downstream aggregation (benchmark-lab runner + sheets) can consume.

This PR adds:
- Quantization mode toggles (baseline|fp8|int8) wired through the harness config, with explicit logging of what was selected.
- Consistent warmup + measurement loops (separate warmup_iters and measure_iters, fixed sampling strategy, optional cooldown between samples).
- A stable artifact export schema (JSON) with required metadata for reproducibility: git SHA, build ID, container image, CUDA + driver versions, GPU name, SM count, clocks (if pinned), model identifier/hash, prompt distribution id, batch size, concurrency, and mode.
- Standardized metric summary output (p50/p95 for TTFT/TPOT where available; tokens/s; GPU util if present) plus per-sample raw points for variance analysis.

Why
The current harness implicitly “warms up” by doing a few iterations but differs between microbench and end-to-end harness entrypoints. This shows up as high variance (especially on H100) and makes it hard to compare kernel changes. Also, we have several one-off artifact formats across scripts; this PR moves us to a single structured output that later PRs can upload and aggregate.

User-facing / operator impact
None. This only affects the internal benchmark harness entrypoints used by runtime perf suite jobs.

Details
1) New config and CLI flags
- Added `--kernel_mode` (baseline|fp8|int8)
- Added `--warmup_iters`, `--measure_iters`
- Added `--sample_count` and `--sample_strategy` (contiguous|interleaved)
- Added `--export_artifact_path` (writes one JSON per run)

2) Warmup/measurement behavior
- Warmup runs are excluded from metrics.
- Measurement runs are sampled into per-sample metrics; summary stats computed across samples.
- Default behavior aligns microbench + e2e harness.

3) Artifact format
- `artifact_version: 1`
- `run_id` stable-ish (timestamp + short git sha)
- `environment` (gpu, cuda, driver, container)
- `workload` (model, prompt set id, batch, concurrency, prefill/decode mix)
- `mode` (baseline|fp8|int8)
- `metrics` (summary + raw)

Example excerpt (illustrative): {"artifact_version":1,"run_id":"2026-02-13T02:41:22Z-1f2c9ab","mode":"fp8","environment":{"gpu":"NVIDIA H100 SXM","cuda":"12.4","driver":"550.54","container":"runtime-bench:1.22.0-rc1"},"workload":{"model":"catalog/llama-70b","prompt_set":"top-hosted-v3-short","batch_size":8,"concurrency":32,"mix":"prefill:30/decode:70"},"metrics":{"ttft_ms":{"p50":112.3,"p95":146.8},"tpot_ms":{"p50":7.9,"p95":10.6},"tokens_per_sec":18432.1,"samples":[...]}}

Out of scope (follow-ups)
- Artifact upload to Drive/warehouse (tracked separately; this PR only writes local artifacts).
- Driver/CUDA pinning + GPU clock locking in the runner (benchmark-lab PR).
- Scheduler instrumentation for prefill/decode mix (ENG-7425 / separate PR).

Test plan
- Unit tests for config parsing + mode dispatch.
- Local run: baseline + fp8 + int8 for a small model (sanity only) to validate artifacts and summaries.
- CI: `runtime-perf-harness-smoke` job runs a minimal harness invocation and asserts artifact contains required fields.

Checklist
- [x] Added flags + documented in `perf_harness/README.md`
- [x] Ensured defaults preserve current behavior for baseline runs
- [x] Added schema versioning (`artifact_version`)
- [x] Added a smoke test to guard against artifact regressions

Commits (squash-merged)
- perf(harness): add kernel_mode and iteration controls
- perf(harness): unify warmup/measure loops and summary stats
- perf(harness): add artifact schema + exporter
- tests: add artifact schema smoke test and CLI parsing coverage
- docs: update harness README with new flags + examples

Files changed (high level)
- runtime/perf_harness/cli.py
- runtime/perf_harness/runner.py
- runtime/perf_harness/measurements.py
- runtime/perf_harness/artifacts/schema_v1.py
- runtime/perf_harness/artifacts/exporter.py
- runtime/perf_harness/README.md
- runtime/tests/perf_harness/test_artifact_schema.py

Review discussion
- Claire Dubois: Can we guarantee warmup is excluded everywhere, including microbench entrypoints? Also please call out defaults clearly to avoid changing historical comparability.
  - Rina Kobayashi: Updated runner to use the same `MeasurementLoop` in both paths; added explicit log line and README note. Defaults match current (warmup_iters=5, measure_iters=30) for baseline; also added `artifact_version` for comparability.
- Marcus Reed: For end-to-end, do we want interleaved sampling to reduce drift (thermals/clock)?
  - Rina Kobayashi: Added `sample_strategy` with `interleaved` option; default remains contiguous for now. We can switch in the matrix runner once we validate noise characteristics.
- Isabella Rossi: Artifact should include model revision/hash and prompt set version so we can diff runs later.
  - Rina Kobayashi: Added `model_id` + `model_sha256` (if available from loader) and `prompt_set_id` + `prompt_set_version` fields.
- Grace Kim: For FP8/INT8 toggles, please make sure the harness records the actual resolved mode after fallback (e.g., unsupported shape).
  - Rina Kobayashi: Added `resolved_mode` in artifact and log; if runtime falls back to baseline it will record `requested_mode` vs `resolved_mode`.

CI / checks
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- lint (ruff/clang-format): pass
- runtime-perf-harness-smoke: pass
- One CI rerun due to flaky timing assertion in smoke test; fixed by asserting presence/shape of fields rather than exact values.

Merge
Merged via squash on 2026-02-13 into main.

Notes
This is intended to be the foundation for the sprint’s benchmark matrix. Please avoid making ad-hoc metric output changes without bumping `artifact_version` (or adding fields in a backward-compatible way).
